newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU trade opt for rapeoil to avoid modified soy - ZMP.
newsitem.headline: EU trade opt for rapeoil to avoid modified soy - ZMP.

text.p: Northern European vegetable oil traders are swapping prefixed soy oil supply orders for rape oil in order to avoid soy oil made from genetically-altered soybeans, a report from Germany's farm price office ZMP said on Thursday.
ZMP said the trend applied to November-March delivery and created a price premium of rape over soy oil.
The November/January premium on Thursday morning was 4.75 guilders per 100 kg fob mill, with soy oil at 95.25 guilders.
ZMP also said there was talk that large processors were interested in securing old soy oil stocks where the use of biotechnology could be ruled out.
This could also boost the soy oil price in the short term.
Genetically-modified soybeans will arrive from the U.S. in the next few months but it is unclear if consumers will accept them.
Environmental group Greenpeace opposes the new products on environmental and political grounds and because it says human health risks cannot be ruled out.
The American Soybean Association and developer Monsanto Co have stressed that the soybeans are safe.
